what_its_for: Primaquine is an antiparasitic medicine used to treat and prevent certain types of malaria, especially a type called Plasmodium vivax malaria. It works by killing the malaria parasites that hide in your liver and can cause the infection to come back weeks or months later. Your doctor may also use it to prevent malaria from returning after you have been treated with another malaria medicine.
how_to_take: Take primaquine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Always take it with food or a full glass of milk to help prevent stomach upset and nausea. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Complete the full course of treatment even if you start to feel better, because stopping early can allow the infection to come back.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of malaria you have, and your overall health. A common adult dose is 15 mg (base) once daily for 14 days, but your dose may be different. For some patients, a higher dose or longer course may be needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store primaquine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any leftover medication.
what_to_avoid: Before taking primaquine, tell your doctor if you have a condition called G6PD deficiency (a hereditary enzyme disorder), as this medicine can cause serious destruction of red blood cells in people with this condition. Avoid taking antacids that contain magnesium or aluminum at the same time as primaquine, as they can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed. Avoid alcohol during treatment, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with primaquine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you notice: dark brown, red, or cola-colored urine; unusual tiredness or weakness; fast heartbeat or shortness of breath; bluish color of the lips, fingernails, or skin; dizziness or fainting; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); severe stomach pain or vomiting; chest pain; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. These can be signs of serious side effects that need immediate medical attention.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within the first few days of treatment, but it is very important to finish the entire course of medicine. Stopping early may allow the malaria parasites to survive in your liver and cause the infection to come back. Your doctor may order blood tests during or after treatment to confirm that the infection has been fully cleared.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Primaquine should NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking primaquine unless your doctor specifically advises it and checks that your baby does not have G6PD deficiency. Children: Primaquine can be used in children, but the dose will be adjusted based on weight. G6PD Deficiency: You MUST be tested for G6PD deficiency before starting primaquine. People with G6PD deficiency can develop a life-threatening breakdown of red blood cells. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as you may need special monitoring or a dose adjustment. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely by their doctor.
